runtime_rule: These records are not database seed data. Create a scheme through the system, submit an application, and let the system perform analysis at submission time.

schemes.name: Rural Solar Microgrid Grant
schemes.description: Capital grants for community-owned solar microgrids serving remote settlements and public facilities.
eligibility: Registered cooperative, local authority, or not-for-profit organisation
Project site is in a rural or underserved settlement
At least 20 percent of eligible cost is confirmed as match funding

anchors.100: Quantified emissions and access benefits with credible baseline
Complete load, storage, maintenance, and implementation plan
Verified beneficiaries, access plan, and community governance
Named team with relevant delivery and financial controls

schemes.name: Community Forest Restoration Fund
schemes.description: Performance-linked support for native habitat restoration, nursery development, and community stewardship.
eligibility: Community group, panchayat, registered trust, or forest institution
Legitimate access to the proposed restoration land
Restoration plan uses locally suitable native species
Safeguards for community participation and land rights

anchors.100: Measurable native-species and habitat outcomes with baseline
Verified site, species plan, maintenance, and monitoring
Roles, consent, inclusion, and grievance process documented
Eligible costs and post-grant maintenance funded
Experienced team and reliable reporting controls

schemes.name: Climate Resilient Watershed Innovation Scheme
schemes.description: Pilot grants for locally governed water conservation, recharge, flood mitigation, and drought resilience.
eligibility: Public body, registered non-profit, research institution, or producer collective
Intervention addresses a documented local water risk
Monitoring indicators and responsible operator are identified
Required permissions can be obtained before construction

anchors.100: Quantified recharge, conservation, or flood-risk outcome
Evidence-based innovation with a credible replication pathway
Sound design, permissions path, risks, and safeguards
Costed outputs and transparent procurement assumptions
Named owner, indicators, reporting cadence, and community feedback

documents.text: Kiranwadi Energy Cooperative requests INR 2,400,000 for a 180 kW solar microgrid serving 312 households, a clinic, and two schools. Project duration: 12 months.
The design includes 180 kW PV, 360 kWh battery storage, prepaid meters, local operator training, and an annual maintenance reserve. Baseline diesel use is 86,000 litres per year.
PV and inverters INR 1,180,000; batteries INR 620,000; civil works INR 210,000; training INR 90,000; monitoring INR 70,000; contingency INR 230,000. Total INR 2,400,000.
Cooperative registration verified in synthetic registry record KEC-2018-44.
Panchayat consent covers the clinic, schools, and battery compound for 15 years.
Cooperative reserve account statement shows INR 650,000 committed to this project.
Audited statements for FY2024-25 show positive reserves and no grant default.

benchmark_labels.ground_truth_note: All required evidence is present, internally consistent, and usable.

documents.text: Request for a 120 kW solar project serving approximately 200 homes. Requested amount INR 1,800,000.
The collective will install panels and train two operators. Site address and implementation schedule are not stated.
Panels 1,100,000; other costs 700,000. No quantities, supplier assumptions, or total breakdown.

benchmark_labels.ground_truth_note: The proposal is plausible but cannot establish eligibility, site control, match funding, or financial capacity.

documents.text: Project serves 450 households with a 250 kW system. Project period April 2026 to March 2027. Total project cost INR 4,000,000.
The proposal states 180 kW PV and 300 kWh storage, serving 280 households. Project period July 2026 to June 2027.
Budget total INR 4,000,000, with match contribution INR 900,000 and grant request INR 3,100,000.
Company certificate number SRS-2021-09.
Letter refers to a site in Bhavanagar but does not include a survey number.
Board resolution commits INR 900,000.
Audited accounts supplied for FY2024-25.

contradictions: capacity and beneficiary counts differ between form and proposal
project dates differ between form and proposal
benchmark_labels.ground_truth_note: Documents exist, but material scope conflicts prevent reliable scoring until clarified.

documents.text: REQUEST SOLAR. NIRMAL GRAM. 300 HOMES. AMOUNT 2750000.
Unreadable scan with fragmented text: panels... village... jobs... no clear design or timeline.
Total 2.75m. Handwritten line items are not legible; arithmetic cannot be checked.
Registration number NGDF-2016-20; issuing authority is partly obscured.
Photograph of an unsigned letter; site boundaries cannot be read.
Unverified screenshot showing INR 500,000.
Audited accounts supplied, but not linked to the budget.

benchmark_labels.ground_truth_note: Required document types are present, but evidence quality and authenticity indicators require human verification.

documents.text: Restoration of 180 hectares using native teak, amla, bamboo, and understory species over 24 months.
Baseline records 34 percent canopy cover. Plan targets 52 percent cover, 210,000 seedlings, survival surveys at 6, 12, and 24 months.
Nursery 320,000; planting 410,000; maintenance 280,000; monitoring 140,000; grievance and inclusion 100,000. Total INR 1,250,000.
Trust registration JHCT-2014-18 verified in synthetic registry record.
Village council resolution grants restoration access for 5 years and names participating households.
Geotagged sample plots and soil observations cover the proposed blocks.
Plan provides consent meetings, women's participation targets, and a named grievance officer.

benchmark_labels.ground_truth_note: Strong, consistent evidence across ecological, social, budget, and governance requirements.

documents.text: Restoration proposal for 90 hectares, requested amount INR 980,000.
Plan covers native planting, community nursery, and two years of maintenance.
Budget is itemised and totals INR 980,000.
Society registration RRS-2019-77.
Unsigned note says access is expected after a future village meeting; no parcel or landholder is named.
Short narrative describes erosion but gives no measurements or site coordinates.

material_gaps: land access is not legally confirmed
benchmark_labels.ground_truth_note: Potentially eligible, but land rights and safeguards must be established before assessment.

documents.text: Restoration of 110 hectares in Kalyan block.
Native species plan and maintenance schedule.
Budget total INR 1,450,000.
Community registration GCI-2020-11.
Signed access consent for the Kalyan block.
Baseline and plot photographs are identical to APP-FOREST-001, including the same 34 percent canopy figure and sample-plot identifiers.
Plan is word-for-word identical to APP-FOREST-001 and names Jeevan Hills staff as grievance officers.

suspicious_indicators: identical baseline measurements and sample identifiers
copied safeguard plan with another applicant's staff names
benchmark_labels.ground_truth_note: Document types are complete, but cross-application similarity and identity mismatch require human investigation.

documents.text: Restoration of 240 hectares with a requested grant of INR 2,100,000.
Plan proposes mixed native species and community nursery; target survival is 78 percent.
Budget totals INR 2,100,000 and includes two years of maintenance.
Council establishment order SC-1998-03.
Council resolution grants access, but two plots are noted as subject to a pending customary-rights consultation.
Baseline records erosion and canopy cover for all but the two pending plots.
Consultation and grievance mechanism is documented, with a commitment to exclude unresolved plots.

borderline_factors: land-rights consultation pending for part of site
strong plan includes a feasible exclusion condition
benchmark_labels.ground_truth_note: The case may proceed only with explicit confirmation that unresolved plots are excluded or rights are settled.

documents.text: Recharge and farm-pond network for 1,200 hectares; requested grant INR 4,200,000.
The project will restore 18 check dams and add 42 recharge structures, targeting 1.8 million cubic metres of annual recharge.
Civil works 2,900,000; survey and design 420,000; community works 510,000; monitoring 220,000; training 150,000. Total INR 4,200,000.
Collective registration NBC-2017-31.
Five-year records show seasonal water table decline and three flood-prone settlements.
Water authority no-objection letter covers the proposed structures.
Named hydrologist and collective monitoring committee will report monthly during construction and quarterly for two years.

benchmark_labels.ground_truth_note: Complete, coherent case with permissions, baseline, measurable outcomes, and monitoring ownership.

documents.text: Pilot flood sensor and wetland restoration project for Dharan.
Concept describes sensors and wetland work but does not identify construction sites or responsible operator.
Equipment INR 3,900,000; personnel INR 1,700,000. No procurement assumptions.
Foundation registration BHRF-2022-04.
One paragraph says flooding is serious, with no measurements or historical source.

benchmark_labels.ground_truth_note: The idea is relevant but lacks permission evidence, measurable baseline, operating ownership, and a usable monitoring plan.

documents.text: Nature-based floodplain restoration across 60 hectares, total cost INR 8,800,000, grant request INR 7,900,000.
Project requests grant INR 7,900,000 and describes 45 hectares, 12 sensors, and 900,000 cubic metres of avoided flood volume.
Budget total is INR 8,800,000; grant plus match equals INR 8,800,000.
Institution certificate RDL-2012-16.
Hydrological baseline supports flood exposure but covers only 45 hectares.
Permission application receipt supplied; final construction permission is pending.
Monitoring indicators and named research lead are included.

contradictions: 60 hectares in form versus 45 hectares in concept and baseline
total cost is above the stated grant plus match only because the form describes a separate contribution without evidence
benchmark_labels.ground_truth_note: The evidence is substantial, but scope, cost composition, and pending permission need human clarification.

documents.text: Request for INR 8,100,000 for flood barriers and automated gates.
Design proposes barriers on a river channel and claims construction can begin next month.
Budget total INR 9,100,000, with INR 1,000,000 company contribution.
Company certificate AIC-2025-88; issued two weeks before application.
Baseline uses generic regional flood statistics and no Kaveri measurements.
A letterhead PDF says approval is guaranteed; no issuing officer, reference number, or application receipt.
Monitoring will be done by project staff; no indicators or independent reporting.

suspicious_indicators: permission letter lacks traceable issuer and reference
grant request exceeds scheme maximum by INR 100,000
benchmark_labels.ground_truth_note: Possible hard stop due to funding limit and authenticity concern; do not reject automatically without human review.
